questions.prompt: What flag creates a VM instead of a container with lxc launch?
questions.explanation: The --vm flag tells LXD to create a virtual machine with its own kernel.

questions.prompt: How do you set limits.cpu=1 and limits.memory=192MiB on an existing instance?
options: lxc config set first limits.cpu=1 limits.memory=192MiB
questions.answer: lxc config set first limits.cpu=1 limits.memory=192MiB
questions.explanation: lxc config set can set multiple key=value pairs in a single command.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between lxc shell and lxc exec?
options: lxc shell opens an interactive session; lxc exec runs a single command
lxc exec opens an interactive session; lxc shell runs a single command
lxc shell only works with VMs
questions.answer: lxc shell opens an interactive session; lxc exec runs a single command
questions.explanation: lxc shell gives you an interactive bash session. lxc exec runs one command and returns.

questions.prompt: Select all valid lxc file subcommands:
questions.explanation: lxc file supports push, pull, and edit. There is no file copy, delete, or mount subcommand.

questions.prompt: What command restores instance 'first' to snapshot 'clean'?
questions.explanation: lxc restore <instance> <snapshot> reverts the instance to the snapshot's state.

questions.prompt: By default, what resources does a container see?
options: Resources defined in the default profile
questions.explanation: Without limits, containers inherit all host resources. nproc and free -m inside a container match the host.
